subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose anonymous Talk activity to plugins

question: Should process-wide Talk lifecycle and speaking-timing observation be available to any installed plugin that self-declares a manifest contract, or only through a registry-approved or owner-scoped capability?
rationale: The patch adds a durable public Plugin SDK contract and the correct authorization model depends on the repository's intended installed-plugin trust boundary, not a mechanical implementation choice.

options.title: Require trusted registry approval
options.body: Make the observer available only when installation or registry metadata supplies a trusted capability, while preserving anonymous event payloads.

options.title: Use owner-scoped observation
options.body: Expose activity only from Talk sessions opened or owned by the requesting plugin, avoiding process-wide cross-session metadata.

options.title: Accept the installed-plugin trust model
options.body: Document that any installed plugin may self-declare process-wide observation and accept that this manifest field is API hygiene rather than authorization.

recommendation.title: Require trusted registry approval
recommendation.body: Make the observer available only when installation or registry metadata supplies a trusted capability, while preserving anonymous event payloads.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest direct history across the current observer proposal and the recently merged shared Talk-session work.
